name: Radiant Kin — Synthetic Family Networks
description: Radiant Kin are mixed human-synthetic chosen-family networks that operate on the principle that synthetic beings deserve genuine kinship bonds, not just legal advocacy. Where Seam Rights argues in policy chambers, Radiant Kin builds family tables: communal dinners, shared housing co-ops, and informal adoption ceremonies where humans formally declare synthetic beings as family members with social (if not legal) weight. The network originated in a Tier 2 community kitchen run by synthetic-human couple Daniyar Seitkali-Voss and the synthetic known as Ember-7, who began hosting Friday meals that grew into a citywide network of 'hearth houses.' Members are identified by a small woven red-and-silver cord worn on the wrist.
cultural_impact: Radiant Kin's hearth house model has created de facto legal complications — several members have named synthetic kin in wills and property documents, triggering court cases that Seam Rights has begun to use as test litigation. The movement has also created genuine social infrastructure for synthetics who lack corporate registration.
locations: The First Hearth (original community kitchen, Tier 2 West)
Radiant Kin House Seven, Milwaukee Corridor
The Open Table (weekly gathering, Shelf border)
story_hooks: A Radiant Kin member dies and leaves property to their synthetic kin — the corporate landlord refuses to recognize the inheritance and the synthetic faces eviction.
A synthetic who has lived as a human family member for years is suddenly recalled by their original manufacturer for a mandatory 'update' that would alter their personality — the family refuses.
A hearth house is infiltrated by a journalist writing an exposé framing Radiant Kin as a dangerous cult — the community must decide how to respond without fracturing.
